review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: It is argued that students who have the best academic performance should be rewarded by their school while others say that rewarding students who show improvements is more important. Personally, I believe that both of them should be equally encouraged.

Admittedly, it is obvious that students who show the best academic results should be rewarded. Initially, as these students have diligently applied themselves to their studies, they deserve their praises and privileges. This may encourage these students and others to study harder to win the rewards, therefore, propelling to towards overall academic gains. Moreover, this kind of competition can be seen in almost aspect of life where only the best individuals are rewarded, student are used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition, allowing them to achieve success in later life.

However, I believe that students who have improvements should also be encouraged. Firstly, if only a few smart students can come first and receive the rewards, this may cause others to think that their effort is futile because they can not surpass those outstanding individuals. In this way, they can prone to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened and gradually lose the incentive to study. Secondly, emphasizing improvements can encourage all students to be diligent in their studies and help students to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves irrespective of how well they have been or are performing, creating the constant desire to outdo themselves. As a result, this can even benefit themselves more than the competitive determination to win against all others.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that rewarding both students having the best academic performance and students who have improvements is equally important.

paragraphs: There is an opinion that with the rapid growth of modern technology, people can see historical objects and works of art easily and public museums and art galleries are unnecessary. Personally, I am of the opposite school of thought.

Admittedly, technology can provide a valuable insight into historical objects and artworks. This is primarily because high-resolution images, three-dimensional reconstructions, virtual reality platforms enable viewers to explore masterpieces and ancient artefacts in remarkable detail without leaving home. To illustrate, Louvre museum in France can offer online collection that helps viewers access to artworks more easily with free or very low charge. In this way, art lovers around the world can enjoy and be motivated to develop an interest in artistic. Moreover, technology can help those who cannot afford and have mobility issues still access a vast range of cultural and historical heritages.

However, there are justifiable reasons to believe that the roles of public museums and art galleries are undeniable. Chief of these is that online experience cannot replicate the direct sensory engagement of seeing an artefact or artwork in person as it can evoke emotions and a sense of authenticity that digital images cannot convey. This can be seen in the way when students see soldier uniforms in a war museum, they can understand suffering that death soldiers and past generations have experienced. Furthermore, museums and galleries are vital cultural hubs, symbolizing the identity of a region. In this way, they are the magnet for tourism and the facilitator of bonding within the community.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that although technology can help people access to cultural and historical heritages more easily, the necessity of public museums and art galleries is undeniable.

In this way, art lovers around the world can enjoy these works and be motivated to develop an interest in art. Moreover, technology can help those who cannot afford museum visits or have mobility issues still access a vast range of cultural and historical heritages.

However, there are justifiable reasons to believe that the roles of public museums and art galleries are undeniable. Chief of these is that online experience cannot replicate the direct sensory engagement of seeing an artefact or artwork in person, which can evoke emotions and a sense of authenticity that digital images cannot convey. This can be seen when students see soldier uniforms in a war museum: they can understand the suffering that fallen soldiers and past generations experienced. Furthermore, museums and galleries are vital cultural hubs, symbolizing the identity of a region. In this way, they are the magnet for tourism and the facilitator of bonding within the community.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that although technology can help people access cultural and historical heritages more easily, the necessity of public museums and art galleries is undeniable.

paragraphs: It is argued that a state ban should be imposed on sport that pose fatal risks to player while others believed that individuals should be free to take part. Personally, I am of the latter school of thought, provided that certain conditions are met.

Admittedly, one might argue that dangerous sports should be prohibited as even a minor error can cause death of participant, say, skydiving. However, this ban is not practical. This is primarily because, in remote locations, such as mountain cliffs have minimal surveillance and control, and it is unrealistic for a police officer follow every individuals in order to prevent them from dangerous activities. In this way, a prohibition exists only on paper and it can drive practice underground, which is harder to ensure basic safety standards.

To add further credence to my assertion, I believe that people should be permitted to do any sport as long as they understand risks and receive sufficient training. To illustrate, if people take part in dangerous sports such as deep-ocean diving, bungee jumping, they should register many reputable clubs that have appropriate equipment and qualified supervision. Moreover, new players should be accompanied by an expert and taught what to do when accidents occur. In this way, they can recognize dangers and respond appropriately. As a result, with proper training and necessary precautions, participation will become safer but no activity entirely risk-free.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that banning is neither practical nor effective and freedom to choose under strict condition of training and awareness are a more realistic approach.

paragraphs: It is often argued that children can learn through their trial and error whereas others believe adults should help them avoid mistakes. Personally, I believe that freedom to make mistake should be encouraged provided that errors do not involve serious danger.

Admittedly, opponents of a trial and error approach often emphasise that most mistakes can be avoidable. For example, knives, fire and electricity are all unnecessary for children to get hurt to learn to be more careful. Moreover, if parents shield their children from harm, they can forestall mistakes, meaning that parents can fulfill their duty. Furthermore, prevent pre-emptively may help children avoid failure. In this way, parents can enjoy peace of mind as they do their best to protect and raise their child.

However, those on other side have their own valid reasoning. Chief among these is that it is unrealistic for parents to be around their children all the time since children should spend their time experiencing with new things meaning that make mistakes is inevitable. Added to this is that children may receive invaluable lessons from dealing with their failure, which may stand children in good stead in later stages of life. Furthermore, if children are shielded by adults from everything, they will grow up overdependent on others and it is an undesirable trait.

Overall, it seems to me that allowing children to learn from mistakes is a good preparation for their future provided that parents intervene and give useful guidance to children on important matters and prevent them from errors that may derail their future.

paragraphs: It is often argued that children can learn through trial and error, whereas others believe adults should help them avoid mistakes. Personally, I believe that the freedom to make mistakes should be encouraged, provided that the errors do not involve serious danger.

Admittedly, opponents of a trial-and-error approach often emphasise that most mistakes can be avoidable. For example, children need not get hurt by knives, fire or electricity to learn to be more careful. Moreover, if parents shield their children from harm, they can forestall mistakes and fulfil their duty. Furthermore, preventing mistakes in advance may help children avoid harm. In this way, parents can enjoy peace of mind as they do their best to protect and raise their child.

However, those on the other side have their own valid reasoning. Chief among these is that parents cannot be around their children all the time; consequently, children may try new things and make mistakes. Added to this is that children may learn invaluable lessons from dealing with their failure, which may stand them in good stead later in life. Furthermore, if children are shielded by adults from everything, they will grow up overdependent on others; it is an undesirable trait.

Overall, it seems to me that allowing children to learn from mistakes is good preparation for their future, provided that parents intervene and give useful guidance to children on important matters and help them avoid errors that may derail their future.

paragraphs: The given bar charts illustrate the amount of three different kinds of emission sources of greenhouse gas in the UK over a two decades period, commencing from 1990.

Overall, there was an increase in the amount of gas emissions while the opposite trend was observed in the case of coal and oil emissions. Also of note is that gas had the highest figures from 2000 onwards.

To elaborate, in 1990, around 220 million tons gas was produced in the UK, with a subsequent growth to 300 million tons in 2000. Conversely, the figures for oil and coal declined from about 270 and 305 million tons respectively to 260 and 250 million tons between 1990 and 2000.

Regarding categories with the latter period of the surveyed timeline, The amount of gas emission in the UK continued grow up, from 300 in 2000 to approximately 320 million tons in 2010, marking the highest point of the entire chart. By contrast, the figures for oil and coal emission steadily decreased, from 260 and 250 million tons to 210 and 190 million tons for the same period of time.

Em cần nói rõ đây là lượng khí thải từ nhiên liệu, không phải lượng gas được sản xuất. Ở giai đoạn 1990–2000, hãy giữ cả nhịp giảm rồi tăng của oil; đồng thời sửa câu mở đoạn sau và kiểm tra đơn vị đi cùng mỗi con số.

paragraphs.text: The bar chart compares the amount of carbon emitted from gas, oil and coal in the United Kingdom between 1990 and 2010, with figures given in millions of tons.

Overall, emissions from gas rose and became the highest of the three by 2000. Coal emissions fell throughout the period, whereas oil ended lower than it began despite a brief recovery in the middle years.

In 1990, around 220 million tons of carbon emissions came from gas, compared with approximately 270 million tons from oil and 310 million tons from coal. By 1995, gas had increased to about 270 million tons and coal had fallen to 280 million tons. Oil also declined, reaching roughly 240 million tons. Five years later, gas reached 300 million tons and overtook the other fuels; oil recovered to around 260 million tons, while coal dropped further to 250 million tons.

Regarding the latter half of the period, emissions from gas continued to grow, reaching around 320 million tons in 2010. By contrast, those from oil decreased from about 260 to 210 million tons between 2000 and 2010. Coal followed a similar downward path, falling from approximately 250 to 190 million tons over the same ten years.

task.text:
WRITING TASK 2
You should spend about 40 minutes on this task.
Some people say history is one of the most important school subjects. Other people think that, in today’s world, subjects like science and technology are more important than history. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your knowledge or experience.
Write at least 250 words.

paragraphs: It is argued that the essence of history is undeniable while others believe that subjects such as science and technology have a more significant role in today's world. Personally, I believe each subject has its own benefits and this opinion is feasible or not depends largely on each country's circumstances.

On the one hand, In countries that are less technology advanced, allocating on science-related subjects can enhance national productivity. This is primarily because, with sufficient financial supports, school can equip modern laboratories and conduct scientific projects; thereby motivating students to spend interest in science. As a result, these students can become competent scientists, researchers and skilled workers in many key sectors of economy, such as agriculture, manufacturing, and healthcare, allowing any nations to progress economically.

On the other hand, In more developed countries, where science and technology are already strong, funding for science education is unnecessary. Moreover, these countries have to deal with other important social problem such as social inequality, a loss of cultural identity, which are issues science alone cannot solve. In this way, history should be promoted as it can help students think deeply, understand different cultures, and better appreciate their own traditions and customs. All of these are important for a balanced society. Furthermore, history can also support science itself. For example, history help scientists understand past achievements and mistakes; therefore, helping them avoid repeating failure and improve scientific research. As a result, if history is ignored, a country will strong in term of science and technology but become weak in social development and human connection.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that history and science have their own advantages for economic and social growth and both of them should be equally promoted.
review.overall: Cô thấy em có ý riêng: nhu cầu mỗi quốc gia có thể khác nhau, và lịch sử còn hỗ trợ cách nghiên cứu khoa học. Em hãy giữ ý này nhưng tránh khẳng định rằng nước phát triển không cần đầu tư khoa học; giáo dục khoa học vẫn cần cập nhật. Hai thân bài cần bàn trực tiếp nên ưu tiên dạy gì ở trường, rồi kết luận rõ vì sao cả hai môn vẫn xứng đáng có chỗ trong chương trình.

paragraphs.text: People disagree about whether schools should give more attention to history or to science and technology. I believe both subjects are necessary, although the balance between them can reflect the needs of a particular society.

Science and technology can be especially valuable where a country is developing its industries and public services. Students who conduct experiments learn to test claims, solve practical problems and work with evidence. When schools provide suitable laboratories and trained teachers, pupils may also discover an interest in engineering, healthcare or agriculture. These skills can later help them contribute to the economy and to services that their communities need. This does not mean that scientific study is useful only in less developed countries: technologies change everywhere, so students in every society need a sound scientific foundation.

History serves a different purpose. By studying earlier decisions, conflicts and social changes, students can understand how present institutions and cultural traditions developed. This may help them recognise injustice, appreciate different perspectives and take part in civic life. History can even support scientific thinking: a researcher who understands earlier discoveries and failed approaches can ask better questions rather than repeat avoidable mistakes. In countries facing social division or the loss of cultural heritage, these benefits deserve particular attention, but they are relevant in all societies.

In conclusion, science and technology prepare students to investigate new problems, while history helps them understand people and the choices that shaped their world. A country may adjust the emphasis as its needs change, but schools should retain both areas and teach students to see how they inform one another.
